title: Early Warning Signs: When to Worry and Investigate?
summary: Some signs call for early medical follow-up (not a diagnosis): limited eye contact, not responding when their name is called after the age of one, not pointing to share interest, relying on gestures instead of speech by the age of two, or losing skills the child had previously acquired (words, movements, social interaction). These are 'red flags' for autism or developmental delay—and early detection (before 3 years) changes the course completely. Trust your instinct: if you feel something 'isn’t right,' consult a doctor immediately.
try_this: This week: Write down in your phone’s notes three things your child does daily (words, gestures, interactions). At the end of the week, review: Has there been any regression? Have new skills emerged? Share the list with your pediatrician at the next visit.
reflection_prompts: Have you ever noticed a regression in a skill your child had mastered? What did you do?
What holds you back from asking the doctor at the first sign of concern? How can you overcome it?
